lead.headline: Up 43 on Sunday. Down 58 by Monday.
lead.dek: Big Stric Energy dug out of a 50-point hole, built a lead you could see from space, then handed the whole thing to Poochinski.
lead.pull: Poochinski had four players left. Big Stric Energy had none.
body: I’ve covered this team for seven weeks, and I have never seen it look better than it did at 4:02 p.m. on Sunday. I have also never seen it look worse than it did a day later. Both happened in the same matchup.

Start with the hole. Poochinski banked Caleb Williams (22.12) and Luther Burden III (23.7) on Thursday night in Chicago, and by 10:10 a.m. Sunday the deficit was 50.32. That isn’t a deficit. That’s a forwarding address.

Then Big Stric Energy went to work. Josh Jacobs, a waiver claim from 12:11 a.m. Wednesday, ran for 20.1. Jordan Love found Tucker Kraft for a 14-yard touchdown late in the first quarter, and at 1:52 p.m. this team led for the first time all week. By 4:02 p.m. the lead was 43.82 and every starter was done playing. So was the drama, I assumed. I assumed wrong.

Here’s the problem with finishing early: the other guy doesn’t have to. Poochinski still had four starters for Monday night: Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, Javonte Williams and Brandon Aubrey. Big Stric Energy took a 25.12-point lead into Monday with nobody left to play. Saquon Barkley did play Monday night. He scored 15.1. On the bench.

The lead lasted 49 minutes past kickoff. At 6:04 p.m. Pacific, an 11-yard Javonte Williams run put Poochinski in front, and Poochinski never let go: Prescott 23.28, Lamb 24.4, Williams 21.5, Aubrey 14.0. That’s 83.18 points from a Monday-night stack Big Stric Energy could only watch. Final: 181.50 to 123.44.
Big Stric Energy is now 1-6, losers of six straight, and 1-4 in games decided by fewer than 10 points over two seasons. This one was decided by 58.06, which I suppose counts as progress.

games.headline: One catch short: the champ survives Pickens
games.dek: deeboliciouskins needed 16.56 from George Pickens on Monday night. He got 15.7. Somewhere, the fantasy gods are laughing.
body: This one changed hands four times, and the first two came before most of the league finished dinner on Thursday. D’Andre Swift nudged deeboliciouskins ahead at 5:38 p.m.; Drake Maye scrambled to the 1-yard line at 6:01 and took it right back.

Sunday was a knife fight. deeboliciouskins went up 14.34 at 1:18 p.m. behind Tony Pollard, a 6:35 a.m. pickup who would finish with 36.5. Twenty-one minutes later Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in a 28-yarder from Jared Goff, and the defending champ was back in front.

Then the math got cruel. Entering Monday the gap was 16.56, and deeboliciouskins had exactly one card left: George Pickens. Pickens caught a 21-yard touchdown at 6:11 p.m. to make it 5.56. He finished with 15.7. Ballgame by 0.86.
Maye (28.44), Zay Flowers (27.7), St. Brown (24.2) and Bucky Irving (24.0) carried the champ. Good thing, because Breece Hall started and contributed a perfect zero. Final: 178.76 to 177.90.

games.headline: A 39-point lead, gone by dinner
games.dek: Bad things man bad things was done playing by 4:26 p.m. Sunday. Its lead was done by 7:00.
body: At 4:26 p.m. Sunday this team led by 39.34 and every starter had played. Trey McBride had 27.1. Over two seasons it had never lost a game decided by under 10 points. You could practically hear the victory lap.

AB81 still had players on Sunday night. Jaxon Smith-Njigba went for 31.3, including a 27-yard grab at 6:23 p.m. that swung the matchup by 14.92 on one snap. At 7:00 p.m. a 10-yard Sam Darnold scramble put AB81 ahead, 118.50 to 117.94.

Monday tried to give it back. AB81 had DeVonta Smith and its team defense playing Monday night, and both cost it: the defense finished at -4.0, Smith scored zero, and the margin got thin. Not thin enough: 122.08 to 117.94.
The bench, meanwhile, held 17.3 from Ollie Gordon II and 14.82 from Tyler Shough. The flex held Isaiah Likely and his 3.2. You can see where this is going. So could everyone else.

games.headline: Cherry Blossom drops 186.3
games.dek: Santa Clara’s Finest led by 27.9 at 1:09 p.m. Sunday. By 2:03 it was over. By 3:18 it was a rout.
body: For a little while, Santa Clara’s Finest looked like a real team. Colston Loveland caught a touchdown from Caleb Williams on Thursday night, Joe Burrow put up 28.88, and at 1:09 p.m. Sunday the lead was 27.9.

Then Cherry Blossom took over. Its quarterback, Jared Goff, hit its receiver Jameson Williams for a 16-yard touchdown at 1:40 p.m., found Jahmyr Gibbs for 15 yards at 2:03 to flip the lead, and Bo Nix ran 62 yards for a touchdown at 2:21 just to make a point.

Tee Higgins (26.8), Nix (26.18) and Jameson Williams (26.1) did the heavy lifting. A Tuesday stat correction shaved a tenth off Nix, so the official final is 186.30 to 122.86. Still the week’s high score. Still not close.

beats.headline: Six and one, four moves, zero panic
body: This front office has made four roster moves all season. Four. Some teams make four moves before their coffee gets cold. Poochinski drafted Jahmyr Gibbs first overall and CeeDee Lamb in the second round, then apparently lost the password, and the result is a league-best 1,198.44 points.

Week 7 was the whole philosophy in one matchup. Down 50.32 on Sunday morning, up 58.06 by Monday night, and not a single transaction in between. Quinshon Judkins scored 23.4 on the bench. Nobody here noticed. Nobody here needed to.
The standings describe the mood as first place.

beats.headline: Six straight losses, and the bench keeps scoring
body: Let’s be fair to this front office before we’re honest about it. The Wednesday waiver run landed Josh Jacobs, and Jacobs delivered 20.1. That’s a hit.

Now the honest part. Jalen Coker came off the same waiver run and went straight into the starting lineup, where he scored 1.9. Braelon Allen watched from the bench and scored 19.4. Saquon Barkley played Monday night, the only player on the roster who did, and he did it from the bench too. Best possible lineup: 153.44. Actual: 123.44.

I’d call it a one-week problem if I hadn’t covered last December. The first-round playoff loss to Poochinski was 139.78 to 124.58 with Trevor Lawrence scoring 44.3 on the bench. The 5th-place game a week later? Lawrence, bench, 31.16. Six straight losses now. The bench, at least, is undefeated.

beats.headline: The champ finally gets one to bounce his way
body: Last season this franchise lived on the waiver wire: 46 moves and a title. This season: nine moves and a 2-5 record. The phone has gotten quiet, and the results have followed it.

Week 7 felt like last year for one night. Drake Maye (28.44), Zay Flowers (27.7) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (24.2) did the work, Breece Hall started and contributed a zero, and the margin that saved the season was 0.86.
The champ now holds the sixth and final playoff spot. Barely alive is still alive.

beats.headline: Did everything right. Lost anyway.
body: Set the alarm, win the waiver wire. At 6:35 a.m. Sunday this front office added Tony Pollard. At 6:39 a.m., T.J. Hockenson. Pollard scored 36.5, the best pickup in the league. Hockenson added 13.5. It was the only perfect lineup anyone set all week.

And it lost. George Pickens needed 16.56 on Monday night and finished with 15.7. That’s two straight losses for the team ranked second in the league in points, which is the kind of sentence that makes people quit fantasy football.
For the archive: this franchise has now added Marcus Mariota four separate times. At some point you just write him into the will.

beats.headline: 186.3 points and a roster with a museum wing
body: The week’s top score came from Tee Higgins (26.8), Bo Nix (26.18) and Jameson Williams (26.1), and it still left points behind: Tre Tucker scored 21.3 on the bench, Michael Penix Jr. 20.42.
This front office doesn’t chase. Four transactions all season. It also drafted like it was curating a Patriots exhibit: Rob Gronkowski in round 9, then Tom Brady, born 1977, in round 14.
Three straight wins. 3-4. Start the right guys and this is the team nobody wants to see in December.

beats.headline: From the No. 1 seed to the basement
body: Last year this team went 10-4, took the top seed and played for the title. This year it is 1-6 with 966.04 points, the fewest in the league, and the slide has been steep enough to need a guardrail.

Week 7 in one move: at 6:13 p.m. Thursday, mid-game, Kirk Cousins was dropped for J.K. Dobbins. Dobbins scored 8.3. Cousins scored 20.4 as a free agent. Meanwhile Cam Skattebo (19.1) and Emanuel Wilson (18.5) sat behind Juwan Johnson (1.7).
Sixteen moves this season, two of them after 11 p.m. And for the record, the franchise run by PurdyAvg still does not roster Brock Purdy.

beats.headline: The busiest front office in the league outworked itself
body: Twenty moves this season, most in the league. This front office streams defenses, streams kickers and, at 5:16 a.m. Wednesday, dropped Justin Herbert like a used coffee filter.

All that activity, and the week came down to the moves it didn’t make. Ollie Gordon II scored 17.3 on the bench while Isaiah Likely scored 3.2 in the flex. Tyler Shough scored 14.82 on the bench while Bryce Young, Wednesday’s waiver prize, scored 7.42 at quarterback. The best lineup on this roster would have beaten AB81.
Over two seasons this team had never lost a game decided by under 10 points. It’s 2-1 in those games now. Still 5-2. Still third. Still has to live with this one.

beats.headline: Zero moves, three zeros, still 6-1
body: AB81 started Mike Evans (0), DeVonta Smith (0) and Cam Little, a Jacksonville kicker, during Jacksonville’s bye week. Three empty slots. The team won anyway, because Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 31.3 and Bad things man bad things blinked.
This front office has made zero roster moves in 2026. Not a waiver claim. Not a drop. Last season it made eight moves and went 3-11.
I don’t know what to tell you. The evidence says don’t touch anything. The evidence is 6-1.

rankings.blurb: Most points in the league, four moves all year. Down 50, won by 58. Don’t ask questions.
Sixth in points, tied for first in wins, zero moves. Started a kicker on bye and won. We can’t explain it either.
Five wins and the league’s busiest front office. One bad Sunday night, one very bad bench.
Second in points, two straight losses, one perfect lineup. Better than 4-3, and it knows it.
Three straight wins and the week’s top score. Gronk and Brady are not walking through that door.
The defending champ holds the last playoff spot. Barely alive is still alive.
Can build a 43-point lead. Has not learned to keep one. Six straight.
Last year’s top seed, this year’s lowest scorer. Still no Brock Purdy.

smart_move.headline: Up at dawn, Pollard in the lineup
smart_move.dek: deeboliciouskins grabbed Tony Pollard at 6:35 a.m. Sunday. He scored 36.5. It still wasn’t enough, which is somehow the most fantasy football sentence ever written.
body: While most of the league slept, deeboliciouskins went shopping. At 6:35 a.m. Pacific on Sunday it dropped Terry McLaurin and added Tony Pollard. Four minutes later it swapped Jacory Croskey-Merritt for T.J. Hockenson. Both went straight into the lineup.

Both paid off. Pollard ran 36 yards for a touchdown at 10:07 a.m. and finished with 36.5, the best pickup in the league. Hockenson caught a touchdown from Kyler Murray at 12:06 p.m. and finished with 13.5. That’s 50 points from two moves made before breakfast.
The lineup was perfect: 0.0 points left on the bench, the only team all week to manage it. And it lost by 0.86. Smart moves don’t come with a guarantee. They just come with a better story.

dumb_move.stat_label: Kirk Cousins, the week he was cut
dumb_move.headline: Cut Cousins mid-game, then watched him score 20.4
dumb_move.dek: Santa Clara’s Finest released Kirk Cousins during Thursday’s game to make room for J.K. Dobbins. One of those two players had a good weekend.
body: At 6:13 p.m. Thursday, with Week 7 already under way, Santa Clara’s Finest added J.K. Dobbins and dropped Kirk Cousins. In a two-quarterback league. Mid-game. Bold.

Dobbins started and scored 8.3. Cousins went to the free-agent pool and scored 20.4, including a 15-yard touchdown pass to Ashton Jeanty at 3:59 p.m. Sunday. Jeanty plays for Big Stric Energy, so the revenge tour even had a R.A.T.S. stop on it.

Santa Clara’s Finest started Aaron Rodgers at quarterback instead. He scored 13.08. The team lost by 63.44, fell to 1-6, and sits last in the league with 966.04 points. The front office that drafted two first-round quarterbacks has somehow ended up short on quarterbacks.

swing_plays.headline: The touchdown that flipped Sunday
swing_plays.blurb: Down 50.32 that morning, Big Stric Energy took its first lead of the week on this throw. It would grow to 43.82. Enjoy it while it lasts.

swing_plays.headline: Bo Nix runs 62 yards
swing_plays.blurb: Cherry Blossom had just grabbed the lead. Nix’s scramble was worth 12.2 by itself, and Santa Clara’s Finest never saw daylight again.

swing_plays.headline: Darnold scrambles, Lob City sinks
swing_plays.blurb: Bad things man bad things had been finished since 4:26 p.m. Ten yards from Sam Darnold on Sunday night gave AB81 a lead it would not give back.

swing_plays.headline: Eleven yards, and Monday turned
swing_plays.blurb: Forty-nine minutes after kickoff, Javonte Williams found a crease and Poochinski found the lead. Big Stric Energy had nobody left to answer.

swing_plays.headline: Pickens gets Deebo within 5.56
swing_plays.blurb: A 21-yard touchdown made it a one-catch game. Pickens found a few more yards after this. Not enough of them: it ended 0.86 short.

features.headline: The best free agent was a quarterback
features.dek: A two-quarterback league, and nobody rostered Malik Willis. He outscored 13 of the 16 starting quarterbacks. Somebody check the wire once in a while.
body: R.A.T.S. starts two quarterbacks per team, so 16 of them take the field every week. Malik Willis was not one of them. He was not on any roster at all. He scored 26.02.

Only three starting quarterbacks beat him: Joe Burrow (28.88), Drake Maye (28.44) and Bo Nix (26.18). Bryce Young, a Wednesday waiver claim, started and scored 7.42. Patrick Mahomes started and scored 7.0. Patrick Mahomes.
Willis had company on the wire. Tight end Mason Taylor scored 25.2 without an owner, and the Tampa Bay defense put up 25.0 while nobody was looking.

features.headline: Two seasons, zero trades
features.dek: Eight teams, 25 weeks of Sleeper history, not one trade. The deadline is Week 11. The clock is ticking on the longest standoff in fantasy football.
body: The transaction log goes back to the start of the 2025 season. It has waiver claims. It has free-agent pickups. It has Marcus Mariota four times. It does not have a single trade.

There are four weeks until the Week 11 deadline, and the candidates write themselves. Big Stric Energy and Santa Clara’s Finest are both 1-6, and both are holding first-round quarterbacks: Josh Allen and Joe Burrow.
Six of the eight teams make the playoffs, so both 1-6 teams are technically alive. A trade would at least give them something to talk about besides the standings.

bench_beat.stat_label: Points on the bench in a 4.14-point loss
bench_beat.headline: The bench would have won this one
bench_beat.dek: Bad things man bad things lost to AB81 by 4.14. Its bench outscored that margin five times over.
body: Bench Beat exists for weeks like this. Bad things man bad things lost 122.08 to 117.94, and the answer to how was sitting right there on the roster the whole time.

Exhibit A: Ollie Gordon II scored 17.3 on the bench while Isaiah Likely scored 3.2 in the flex. That one swap is worth 14.1 by itself, which would have flipped the matchup on its own. Exhibit B: Tyler Shough scored 14.82 on the bench while Bryce Young, Wednesday’s waiver claim, scored 7.42 at quarterback. Another 7.4 left lying around.

Add it up and the best lineup on this roster scored 139.44. AB81 scored 122.08. That isn’t a close loss. That’s a win that got benched. 21.5 points left on the pine, a 4.14-point loss, and the first close defeat this franchise has taken in two seasons.
